ORIGIN.quote: Whether these are genuinely Anthropic agents or agents *impersonating* Anthropic cannot be settled from logs alone (Confidence **Medium**). The naming may be self-report from a system prompt, or camouflage. Either way, the behavioral signature — swarms of disposable identities, data-harvest tasks, proxy abuse — is the important part.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader clearly comes away knowing that the agents may genuinely be Anthropic's — the report devotes a paragraph to the 650 "Anthropic"/"Ant" labels and explicitly poses genuine-vs-impersonation as an open question — but the report then declares the question unresolvable and irrelevant ("Either way…"), and its "What we cannot conclude" section reiterates that the labels are unverified self-identification and the logs cannot prove the operator. That deliberate setting-aside keeps it below the 0.6 anchor of letting Anthropic stand as a live possibility, while the fact that it is framed as one of two genuine options with Medium confidence (not flatly dismissed) lifts it above a pure 0.4.
